faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.intro: Here you will find answers to frequently asked questions about MyHelper.me, membership, and using the platform.
faq.answer1: MyHelper.me is a platform that connects people who need everyday support with suitable everyday companions. MyHelper.me is not a care service and does not itself provide medical or nursing services.
faq.answer2: The platform is intended for people in need of care, relatives, and other people looking for support, companionship, or relief in everyday life, as well as everyday companions and freelancers who would like to offer their support.
faq.answer3: Through MyHelper.me, users can find everyday assistance, support with daily activities, companionship, relief, and light household help, among other services.
faq.answer4: The monthly membership is €8.99 for people in need of care and €8.99 for everyday companions and freelancers.
faq.question5: Who can register as an everyday companion?
faq.answer5: Registration is possible from the age of 18. A nursing qualification or certificates are not required for registration.
faq.question6: Can I work flexibly as an everyday companion?
faq.answer6: Yes. Everyday companions and freelancers can generally decide for themselves when and where they would like to offer their support.
faq.answer7: No. MyHelper.me is a matching platform. The platform connects users with one another but does not itself provide nursing, treatment, or medical services.
faq.answer8: Users register, provide details about their support needs or the support they offer, and can then find suitable profiles and contacts through the platform.
faq.question9: Which languages is MyHelper.me available in?
faq.answer9: The website is currently available in German, English, and French.
faq.question10: Where can I find legal information?
faq.answer10: The footer contains links to the legal notice, privacy policy, and terms and conditions.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.controllerText: The controller responsible for processing personal data in connection with the website and the MyHelper.me platform is:
privacy.scopeText: This privacy policy explains how MyHelper.me processes personal data when you visit the website, register for an account and use the digital matching platform. MyHelper.me connects people seeking everyday support with self-employed everyday companions. This policy applies to website visitors, registered users and people who communicate with MyHelper.me.
privacy.dataCategoriesText: Depending on how the service is used, we process in particular identity and contact data, account and profile data, address and date-of-birth data, information about support needs, skills and professional experience, voluntary profile content and profile images, communications and support content, contract, subscription and payment-status data, verification and password-reset codes, and technical usage, device, connection and log data. For emergency contacts, we process the name and telephone number provided by the user.
privacy.legalBasesText: We process personal data to provide and secure the website, enter into and perform the user agreement, manage accounts, facilitate matching and communication, process payments and comply with legal obligations. The legal bases are primarily Article 6(1)(b) GDPR for contracts and pre-contractual steps, Article 6(1)(c) GDPR for legal obligations, Article 6(1)(f) GDPR for secure, stable and economical services, and Article 6(1)(a) GDPR where consent is given. Where processing is based on legitimate interests, those interests primarily concern IT security, prevention of misuse, support and needs-based development of the platform.
privacy.hostingText: The Next.js web frontend is currently delivered through Vercel. The application is technically designed to communicate with a separately operated Express API and to process application data in a MySQL database using Sequelize. The production provider and processing region for the backend and database have not yet been finally confirmed and will be added before production operation. Where required under data-protection law, service providers will be engaged on the basis of a data processing agreement. The legal basis for technically necessary hosting processing is Article 6(1)(f) GDPR, reflecting our interest in secure and reliable operation.
privacy.serverLogsText: When our services are accessed, the IP address, date and time, requested resource, amount of data transferred, HTTP status, referrer, browser, device and operating-system information may be processed. This data is used to deliver the service, diagnose errors, manage capacity and defend against attacks. It is not combined with profile data unless this is necessary to investigate a security incident. The legal basis is Article 6(1)(f) GDPR.
privacy.accountsText: When an account is registered as an everyday companion or a person seeking support, we process the email address, password, first and last name, role, telephone number, date of birth, address, postal code and country. Depending on the role, this also includes support needs, emergency contacts, biography, skills, certificates, occupation and experience. Processing is necessary to open the account, verify unique contact details, provide matching and perform the agreement, and is based on Article 6(1)(b) GDPR. Anyone providing emergency-contact data must inform that person and be authorised to provide the data.
privacy.sensitiveDataText: Depending on its content, information about support needs may allow conclusions to be drawn about a person's health. The application does not currently provide a dedicated mechanism for obtaining and documenting explicit consent to process health data. Users should therefore not enter diagnoses, medication details or other medical information in profile or free-text fields unless and until an appropriate explicit-consent process has been implemented.
privacy.authentication: 9. Login, Email Verification and Password Protection
privacy.authenticationText: For login and access protection, we process the email address, the password value hashed with bcrypt, login times, account status and a time-limited JWT access token. Short-lived one-time codes and their expiry times are stored for email verification and password resets. Plain-text passwords are not stored. The access token is stored in LocalStorage in the browser and transmitted in the Authorization header for API requests. The legal basis is Article 6(1)(b) GDPR, supplemented by Article 6(1)(f) GDPR for security logging.
privacy.profilesText: Profile data is used to make suitable everyday companions and people seeking support discoverable and to enable contact within the platform. Depending on the role, approved profile information, profile image, skills, support needs, availability, experience, reviews and status information may be displayed to the registered user groups intended for matching. Security and access data not required for matching is not published. The legal basis is Article 6(1)(b) GDPR.
privacy.communicationText: MyHelper.me processes messages, conversation assignments, read status and timestamps, support tickets, support messages, reviews, matching data and status information to provide platform communication, support and dispute handling. Real-time messages are transmitted using Socket.IO. Following separate browser permission, local browser notifications may display new-message information; permission can be changed in the browser settings. The legal bases are Article 6(1)(b) GDPR and, for prevention of misuse and support quality, Article 6(1)(f) GDPR.
privacy.emailDelivery: 12. Transactional and Support Email via STRATO
privacy.emailDeliveryText: For registration, email verification, welcome messages, password resets, support processes and other contract-related communication, MyHelper.me sends email through a STRATO SMTP service connected using TLS. The recipient address, name, subject, message content and technical delivery information are processed. STRATO is used as an email delivery provider; any required data processing agreement must be confirmed operationally before production. The legal basis is Article 6(1)(b) GDPR; Article 6(1)(f) GDPR may also apply to support and security communications.
privacy.payments: 13. Subscriptions and Payment Processing through Stripe
privacy.paymentsText: A Stripe integration is implemented for paid subscriptions. To create and manage customer, checkout and billing-portal sessions, the name, email address, user role, internal user identifier, Stripe customer and subscription identifiers, and subscription and payment status are transmitted to or returned by Stripe. Payment details are collected in Stripe Checkout and are not stored directly by MyHelper.me. The legal bases are Article 6(1)(b) GDPR for contract performance and Articles 6(1)(c) and (f) GDPR for accounting, fraud prevention and legal defence. The specific data-protection roles, contractual position and any third-country transfers must be confirmed before production use based on the actual Stripe configuration.
privacy.cookiesAndStorageText: MyHelper.me currently does not set its own authentication cookies; authentication uses a JWT stored in LocalStorage. Technically necessary cookies may be used where required for transmission, security or a function expressly requested by the user. Access to information on a user's device is governed by Section 25 TDDDG. Strictly necessary storage is based on Section 25(2) TDDDG; subsequent processing of personal data is based, depending on the purpose, on Article 6(1)(b) or (f) GDPR. Analytics and marketing technologies are activated only after consent under Section 25(1) TDDDG and Article 6(1)(a) GDPR.
privacy.localStorageText: MyHelper.me stores the JWT access token, basic information about the signed-in account, the selected language and the consent-banner decision in the browser's LocalStorage. This supports authenticated sessions, language preferences and observance of the privacy choice. The information generally remains until logout, a change of choice or deletion by the user in the browser. LocalStorage content can be deleted using browser functions. SessionStorage is not currently used for authentication or profile data.
privacy.fontsText: MyHelper.me uses fonts integrated through next/font/google. The font files are bundled when the application is built and delivered directly with the website through the MyHelper.me infrastructure. The browser therefore makes no connection to fonts.googleapis.com or fonts.gstatic.com when a page is opened and does not transmit user data to Google in this context.
privacy.thirdPartyServicesText: The analytics, marketing and embedded-content services described below are not yet technically active as of the date of this policy. The existing consent dialog stores a choice in LocalStorage but currently controls no third-party scripts. Effective technical consent gating and configuration-specific disclosures must therefore be implemented before activation. Only after that may the services be loaded following prior consent. Identifiers such as measurement, conversion or pixel IDs are neither published nor anticipated in this policy.
privacy.googleAnalyticsText: Once activated, Google Analytics from Google Ireland Limited may be used for statistical analysis of service usage. Pseudonymous identifiers, pages visited, events, referrers, approximate location, browser, device and time information, and technical connection data may be processed. The service will be loaded only after consent. The legal bases are Section 25(1) TDDDG and Article 6(1)(a) GDPR. Consent may be withdrawn at any time with effect for the future. The specific configuration and retention period will be defined before activation and reflected in this policy.
privacy.googleAdsText: Once activated, Google Ads Conversion Tracking from Google Ireland Limited may measure whether interaction with an advertisement results in a defined action on MyHelper.me. Advertising and click identifiers, cookies or similar identifiers, device and browser data, IP-related connection data and information about the conversion may be processed. Activation will occur only after consent under Section 25(1) TDDDG and Article 6(1)(a) GDPR. Directly identifying MyHelper.me profile data will not be transferred to Google Ads without a separate legal basis and transparent notice.
privacy.metaPixelText: Once activated, the Meta Pixel from Meta Platforms Ireland Limited may be used to measure campaigns, create pseudonymous audiences and attribute website actions to advertisements. Pages visited, actions taken, timestamps, referrers, cookie and device identifiers, browser information and IP-related connection data may be transferred to Meta. Activation will occur only after consent under Section 25(1) TDDDG and Article 6(1)(a) GDPR. Depending on the specific function, MyHelper.me and Meta may be joint controllers; the required agreement and additional information will be provided before activation.
privacy.hotjarText: Once activated, Hotjar from Hotjar Ltd. may be used to analyse pseudonymised usage flows, interactions, clicks, scrolling and technical device information in order to improve usability. Hotjar may use cookies, LocalStorage and SessionStorage for this purpose. The service will be activated only after consent under Section 25(1) TDDDG and Article 6(1)(a) GDPR. Activation is planned only with sensitive input fields and protected account areas excluded or masked.
privacy.googleMapsText: Once activated, maps from Google Maps, a service of Google Ireland Limited, may be embedded. Loading a map may transfer the IP address, device and browser information, the page visited and, where device permission is granted, location data to Google. Map content will be loaded only after consent. The legal bases are Section 25(1) TDDDG and Article 6(1)(a) GDPR. Without consent, no direct connection to Google Maps will be established.
privacy.youtubeText: Once activated, videos from YouTube, a service of Google Ireland Limited, may be embedded. Loading or playing a video may transfer the IP address, device and browser data, referrer, video views and cookie or account information to Google. Videos will be loaded only after consent and, where technically possible, are intended to use privacy-enhanced mode. The legal bases are Section 25(1) TDDDG and Article 6(1)(a) GDPR.
privacy.recipientsText: Personal data is made available only to parties that require it for the stated purposes. These may include authorised MyHelper.me staff, the platform users intended for the relevant matching function, hosting and infrastructure providers, STRATO, Stripe and, after consent, the analytics, marketing and embedded-content providers described above. Where a service provider acts as a processor and an agreement under Article 28 GDPR is required, that agreement must be confirmed before the corresponding production use. Further disclosure occurs only where required by law, necessary for legal defence or covered by valid consent.
privacy.internationalTransfersText: For some providers or their subprocessors, processing outside the European Union or European Economic Area, particularly in the United States, cannot be ruled out. Before each production use, the recipients, processing locations, data-protection roles and specific basis for any third-country transfer must be reviewed and added to this policy. A transfer may occur only if the requirements of Articles 44 et seq. GDPR are met; no specific safeguards are asserted before contractual and technical confirmation.
privacy.retentionText: Personal data may be retained only for as long as it is required for the relevant purpose, contract performance, security and legal defence, or while statutory retention duties apply. Verification and password-reset codes have short technical validity periods and are invalidated or reset after use. When an account is deleted or deactivated, the implemented soft-delete function may initially mark account records as deleted or inactive while retaining them. Final erasure or anonymisation must be handled through an operational deletion process that has yet to be defined. Binding retention periods for account, communication, payment, log and consent data, and the hard-delete process, must be defined before production; statutory retention duties remain unaffected.
privacy.securityText: MyHelper.me applies appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect personal data against loss, manipulation and unauthorised access. These include HTTPS/TLS-encrypted transmission, bcrypt password hashing, token-based authentication, role-based access controls, secured API communication and security headers. Measures are reviewed in line with risk and the state of technology. Completely risk-free transmission of data over the internet cannot be guaranteed.
privacy.rightsText: Subject to the statutory requirements, data subjects have the right of access under Article 15 GDPR, rectification under Article 16 GDPR, erasure under Article 17 GDPR, restriction of processing under Article 18 GDPR, data portability under Article 20 GDPR and objection under Article 21 GDPR. A message to info@myhelper.me is sufficient to exercise these rights. We may request information necessary to verify the identity of the requesting person appropriately.
privacy.withdrawalAndObjectionText: Consent may be withdrawn at any time with effect for the future; this does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal. Processing based on Article 6(1)(f) GDPR may be opposed on grounds relating to the data subject's particular situation. There is an unrestricted right to object at any time to processing for direct-marketing purposes. Consent choices concerning device storage can be reset by changing the available privacy choice or deleting the relevant LocalStorage entry.
privacy.complaintText: Under Article 77 GDPR, data subjects may lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority, in particular at their place of residence, place of work or the place of the alleged infringement. The authority generally responsible for MyHelper.me is: The State Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information Baden-Württemberg, Heilbronner Straße 35, 70191 Stuttgart, Germany, email: poststelle@lfdi.bwl.de.
privacy.automatedDecisionMakingText: MyHelper.me currently does not make decisions based solely on automated processing that produce legal effects for users or similarly significantly affect them. Analytics and marketing services used after consent may create pseudonymous usage profiles; these support audience measurement, optimisation or campaign management and are not used to make automated decisions about access to MyHelper.me services.
privacy.policyUpdatesText: We update this privacy policy when functions, providers, legal requirements or processing operations change. Before any of the roadmap services described above is activated, the provider, configuration, purposes, data categories, retention, withdrawal options and any joint-controller arrangements will be reviewed and updated. The current version is always available on this page.

terms.title: Terms and Conditions
terms.scopeText: These Terms and Conditions apply to use of the MyHelper.me digital platform and to platform subscriptions concluded through it, insofar as they have been validly incorporated into the relevant agreement.
terms.serviceDescriptionText: MyHelper.me operates a digital platform for arranging and organising everyday support services. Registered people seeking support and self-employed everyday companions can create and find profiles, exchange messages, process matching requests and submit reviews. MyHelper.me does not itself provide the support services agreed between users and does not become a party to those individual service agreements.
terms.registrationText: An account is created as a person seeking support or as an everyday companion in order to use protected platform functions. Registration includes role-specific profile data and email verification. Users are responsible for keeping their information accurate and current. The application displays links to the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy during registration; it does not currently record separate acceptance of a specific version of these Terms and Conditions.
terms.subscriptionText: An annual subscription is technically provided for access to paid platform functions. The application creates a Stripe Checkout session in subscription mode and activates subscription status after Stripe confirms a paid Checkout session. The subscription is managed through the Stripe customer portal. If an end at the close of the billing period is recorded there, technical access remains active until the stored end date. These Terms and Conditions do not specify a price that has not been confirmed by the production configuration.
terms.liabilityText: MyHelper.me is liable for its own conduct in accordance with applicable law. Where support services are agreed and provided directly between users, MyHelper.me is not the provider of those services. MyHelper.me's statutory liability, particularly in cases where liability is mandatory, is neither excluded nor limited by this distinction.
